findings.location: src/db/org.ts:895-907 (loadAdminContext step 3, the per-role delegable mgmt_object:* grant query) vs the canonical grant-active gate in src/db/grants-dao.ts:388-404 (getGrantsForSubject step 3)
findings.issue: CONFIRMED, and materially stronger than the task's own '§6 real-looking' framing: this is a REACHABLE (live), not merely dormant, dual-control gap — but on a DIFFERENT axis than T-0767 was scoped to. loadAdminContext step 3 selects `mgmt_object:%` delegable grants with ONLY `delegable=true AND resource_type LIKE 'mgmt_object:%' AND window` — NO `confirmed_by`, NO `criticalGrantPredicate/confirmed2_by`. The canonical PDP getGrantsForSubject step 3 enforces `confirmed_by IS NOT NULL AND (NOT <criticalGrantPredicate> OR confirmed2_by IS NOT NULL)`. Divergence is live-reachable: the /api/grants propose path (src/http/grants.ts:928 escalating branch) INSERTs a delegable mgmt_object:* grant whose resource_type/operation/delegable come straight from the request body; an operation IN ('approve','transition') (e.g. mgmt_object:tier_promote/transition, consumed by artifacts.ts:232) is CRITICAL by criticalGrantPredicate axis-a, so it lands SEMI-CONFIRMED (confirmed_by=actor, confirmed2_by=NULL). getGrantsForSubject filters that row OUT; loadAdminContext step 3 returns it in adminGrants, so every consumer that gates on `admin.adminGrants.some(...)` (artifacts.ts, secret-handle.ts, llm-config.ts, seed-write.ts, agents.ts via validateAdminDelegation, notification-prefs, report-pages, registry-defs, email-channel-config) would authorize on ONE approver — the exact second-signature bypass dual-control exists to stop. CRUCIALLY this is the T-0397/T-0044 GRANT-row confirmation axis, NOT the T-0605 ASSIGNMENT-row axis this task was scoped to (the finding handed down from T-0764 review §3.2). It is pre-existing, untouched and un-worsened by this diff, and fixing it needs a real design decision (are all delegable mgmt_object:* grants 'critical'? 'apply'/'create'/'update' are NOT critical under the current predicate, so it is not a one-liner). The task found it, characterized the axis correctly, and deferred it in spec.md §6 under D-064 anti-scope-creep discipline — the desired behavior, not a defect of this PR. NON-BLOCKING because it is a separate finding on a separate axis (the T-0767 finding IS fully closed), but flagged HIGH-priority because it is reachable today, unlike the (truly dormant) T-0605 axis this task fixed.
findings.suggestion: File a dedicated HIGH-priority follow-up (grant-row dual-control axis): route loadAdminContext step 3 through the same grant-active predicate getGrantsForSubject step 3 uses — `AND confirmed_by IS NOT NULL AND (NOT ${CRITICAL_GRANT_PREDICATE_BARE} OR confirmed2_by IS NOT NULL)` on choros."grant" — after deciding the mgmt_object:* criticality classification (T-0040/T-0044). Add a db-tier probe seeding a semi-confirmed critical delegable mgmt_object:tier_promote/transition grant and asserting it does NOT appear in adminGrants and does NOT authorize the artifacts/secret-handle consumers.

BUT none of them is a grant-PDP-short-circuit AUTHORITY resolver of the isGenesisOwnerForTenant/loadAdminContext class the finding was about, so this is NOT a недозакрытие of the finding: findTenantOwnerSlug/findTenantOwnerEmployeeId are task-routing / notification-recipient fallbacks; getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee bounds (narrows) a Tier-2 substitution rule to the ABSENT holder's own scope; rights-sod.ts is held-roles DISPLAY; sod-dao effectiveAssignmentsOf feeds SoD conflict detection (over-inclusion = more-restrictive = safe direction); the user-mgmt last-owner guards COUNT owners for a fail-closed safety guard, not to grant authority. All are DORMANT (no live write path sets role_assignment.proposed_by non-null — T-0764's 58-seed audit, re-confirmed). The one authority gate among them, binding.ts:210 (process_designer), has a DIFFERENT pre-existing gap (no confirmed_by and no window at all), unrelated to the T-0605 disjunct. capability-grants-dao (canConfigureLlmConnection/canActorOperateSystemAgents) delegates to getGrantsForSubject/loadAdminContext, so it inherits this fix. Conclusion: the finding is fully closed on its axis; these are optional consistency hardening.
findings.suggestion: Optional, non-blocking: when the assignment-level propose/escalate feature is actually built, sweep these same-class reads onto assignmentActiveDualControlPredicate too (findTenantOwner* and getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee are the closest to authority-relevant).
